description: The line plot illustrates the training loss over training steps for six different model configurations—ChemBART Small 20M, ChemBART Medium 20M, ChemBERTa Small 20M, ChemBERTa Medium 20M, ChemLLaMA Small 20M, and ChemLLaMA Medium 20M—all trained on a 20 million data point dataset. The x-axis, labeled “Step,” spans from 0K to 440K in linear scale, with major tick marks at 0K, 20K, 40K, 60K, 80K, and then zoomed-in ticks at 420K, 430K, and 440K, indicating a focus on the final convergence phase. The y-axis, labeled “Train Loss,” ranges from 0.0 to 0.85 in linear scale, with major gridlines at 0.0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.75, and 0.85. All six lines begin near 0.85 at 0K steps and exhibit a rapid initial decline in loss, followed by a slower, more gradual decrease toward convergence. The ChemBERTa Small 20M model (green line with circular markers) shows the steepest early decline, reaching approximately 0.15 by 440K steps. The ChemLLaMA Medium 20M model (brown line with circular markers) achieves the lowest final loss of approximately 0.01 at 440K steps, consistently outperforming ChemBART Medium 20M (blue line with circular markers), which stabilizes around 0.08. ChemBART Small 20M (red line with circular markers) declines more slowly than ChemLLaMA Small 20M (purple line with circular markers), ending at approximately 0.25 compared to ChemLLaMA Small’s ~0.10 at 440K steps. All lines exhibit some stochastic noise, particularly in the early and mid-training phases, but stabilize in the final 20K steps.
caption_used: Training Loss vs. Steps for Each Model Type by Model Size with a Data Size of 20 million. The loss trends for 10 million and 20 million datasets are similar. The ChemBERTa Small 20M model exhibits the steepest decline in training loss, reaching approximately 0.15 at 440k steps. ChemLLaMA Medium 20M consistently outperforms ChemBART Medium 20M, achieving the lowest loss of all models at 0.01. The ChemBART Small 20M model shows a slower rate of decline compared to ChemLLaMA Small 20M, stabilizing at around 0.25 at 440k steps.
